items.title: Devin Sisak, Barrier-free Cambridge
notes:
D. Sisak provided a presentation on the misrepresentation of low-speed electric vehicles as mobility devices. A copy of the presentation is attached to the addendum agenda. 

Responding to Council, D. Sisak explained that there is a harmony tracking system that identifies the low-speed electric vehicles which are identified differently than mobility devices and mobility devices are not tariffed. 

In response to Council, D. Spooner, Commissioner of Transportation, confirmed that staff will investigate information on the use of low-speed electric vehicles and will report back on the findings by December 2026. The report will include an evaluation of what defines a mobility device and staff will consult with area municipalities.

items.title: Robert Buchanan, Waterloo
notes:
R. Buchanan expressed concern that there was a joint agreement between City of Waterloo and the Region of Waterloo to perform landscaping maintenance on roadways at night. He provided a summary of two separate instances of 40-minute periods when the maintenance was completed at night. He further expressed concern that the maintenance is intrusive to the community and worse for the environment with the use of gasoline fed machines. 

Council expressed concern about the nighttime maintenance due to the time of day, safety for workers, and the potential damage to vehicles. D. Spooner confirmed that staff will report back and will continue to explore options for completing the maintenance in manner that is safe and less intrusive to the community.

items.title: Advancing Truth & Reconciliation (Staff Presentation)
notes:
Paula Whitlow, Director of Truth & Reconciliation, and Stephanie Bryenton, Respectful Workplace Program Manager, performed a smudging ceremony.

Mathieu G, Acting Chief Administrative Officer, introduced a presentation on the Region's work towards Truth and Reconciliation throughout the community and the organization. He explained that this work involves taking intentional steps to address the Truth and Reconciliation Commission's calls to action. The intentional steps include celebrating Indigenous languages, history, and culture, developing safe spaces. He highlighted in importance of the four "Rs" of reconciliation and their role in the strategic plan. 

P. Whitlow highlighted that delivering culturally safe programs and services is a commitment to collaborating with Indigenous community members and organizations to design services and programs that reflect Indigenous cultures, knowledge, and wisdom. Building services that are safe, culturally appropriate, inclusive, and empowering for Indigenous people is an integral step in reconciliation. She provided various examples include supporting Indigenous-led childcare that reflects traditional culture, knowledge, and wisdom; affordable housing supports and rent supplements for Indigenous individuals and families; culturally informed harm reduction and healing services; Indigenous-led healthy child development programs, and collaborations with Indigenous led organizations and youth to address mental health, sustainable food access and more. 

Children’s Services has built and supported a relationship with Healing of the Seven Generations, who opened Gad'nigǫhi:yo Indigenous Child Care and Family Centre, the community’s first Indigenous-led licensed child care program. The centre in Cambridge is licensed for 70 childcare spaces prioritized for First Nations, Inuit, and Métis children aged 0-4. 

Eric Tincombe, Museum Exhibits Researcher, provided an update on the creation of a new outdoor Indigenous space and publicly accessible natural area near the Region of Waterloo International Airport through co-stewardship with Indigenous partners. The area includes 18 Indigenous archaeological sites where cultural belongings recovered indicate the area has been inhabited for at least 10,000 years. He highlighted the next phase will include the selection of an Indigenous-led landscape architecture firm to work with interest holders for engagement throughout the initiative, the establishment of an Indigenous Advisory Committee for the initiative and engage with community to establish appropriate design elements and themes, and determine the estimated cost of the project of approximately $44,800 plus honorariums included in existing Airport Capital Program.

In response to Council, Julian Kingston, Director of Cultural Services, and P. Whitlow confirmed that the initiatives have been in direct consultation with Indigenous groups to ensure that the projects adhere to the strategic priority of Truth and Reconciliation and are culturally significant.

Responding to Council, Peter Sweeney, Commissioner of Community Services, explained that the housing project referenced in the report is the partnership with the KW Native Urban Wigwam building Indigenous-led and Indigenous focused supportive housing. P. Whitlow confirmed that she has been working with Community Services to integrate Indigenous spaces in the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness.

items.title: Other Matters Under Committee Of The Whole
PDL-CUL-25-022, Culture Drivers of Tourism Additional Grant Allocation
notes:
J. Kingston provided a brief overview of report PDL-CUL-25-022, Culture Drivers of Tourism Additional Grant Allocation. He explained that Council directed staff to provide options on how to restore annual funds to the historical funding level of $65,000 for Oktoberfest, including the possibility of using the Regional portion of the MAT for this purpose in 2025. He noted that staff recommended restoring the funding amount to the Cambridge Scottish Festival for consistency as they were the only two organizations not to receive the full amount requested.

Council expressed concerns that the recommendation did not adhere to the direction from Council by restoring the funding to the Cambridge Scottish Festival. Council discussed and debated the inclusion of the Cambridge Scottish Festival in restoring the historical funding allocation. The recommendation was amended to separate the organizations, and they were voted on separately.
